tips.title: Proper Use of Tamiya Basic Nippers
tips.text: Tamiya Basic Nippers are a versatile tool for modelers. They're great for thicker gates but can damage delicate parts if twisted. Always cut straight through, never twisting or pulling. For thicker parts like ICM or Meng sprues, use these nippers; for thinner gates, opt for GodHand Ultimate Nippers.

tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: RB Productions tools have varying depths to accommodate different panel line sizes. For best results, use the tool corresponding to your kit's panel line depth. Apply gentle, steady pressure while moving the tool along the panel line. Start from the center and work outwards to avoid damaging the part.

tips.title: Using Photo-Etch Bending Jigs
tips.text: Eduard photo-etch bending jigs help create consistent bends. Place the photo-etch part over the jig, with the edge you want to bend along the groove. Using tweezers, gently bend the part over the jig's edge. For tighter bends, use the smaller jigs. Always bend before painting to avoid damaging decals.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning Techniques
tips.text: Iwata airbrush needles can clog with dried paint. To clean, soak the needle in Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for 15 minutes, then use an Iwata Airbrush Needle Cleaning Brush to scrub the inside gently. Rinse with water and dry thoroughly before reassembling. Do this regularly to maintain airbrush performance.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs. Kabuki Tape
tips.text: Tamiya Tape is ideal for masking large, flat areas due to its adhesive strength. Kabuki Tape is softer, better for masking curves and edges without pulling paint. For best results, use Tamiya Tape for large areas and Kabuki Tape for intricate curves, like when masking around windows or canopies in Arma Hobby kits.
